prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single B046 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, and the chair's summary shows that every member places the doubt in attribution and none in merit or maturity. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action in humans, Drucker established proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor action and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov's work concerns the identity of the biologically active peptide. That is a physiological discovery with decades of independent confirmation, followed by randomised evidence on glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. A citation tied to physiology and the active form describes what was discovered. It does not require the committee to name a product. The three-person cap makes one part the honest choice here, because a second part would require removing a B046 name whose contribution I regard as necessary to the discovery.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection remains credit. Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested, Habener is outside the credited names, and leaving out Knudsen means that the work that produced durable analogues is not recognised. If the committee judges that the essential achievement is the drug and not the hormone, my trio is incomplete and Knudsen belongs in it. A second objection is that a one-part prize leaves unrewarded another mature mechanism-to-therapy achievement, most obviously CAR-T. I accept that cost, because I do not think it justifies cutting one of the three physiological discoverers, and because the CAR-T credit is itself unsettled with Eshhar outside the list.

responses.point: The chair moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because five colleagues put physiology and peptide identification ahead of analogue development, and asks in the round-2 questions whether Mojsov or Habener has the stronger documented claim.
responses.response: I agree with where you ended up, and I want to be clear about the limits of my reasoning. From the supplied record I cannot show that Mojsov's claim is stronger than Habener's. What I can say is that the committee has no evidence that her contribution to defining the active peptide is weaker than the contributions of Drucker and Holst, and removing her because the dispute exists would settle it by default. If the committee later decides that the record does not support her, I would not move to Knudsen automatically. I would then ask whether the citation should rest on Drucker and Holst with a different third name, and that would be a new discussion and not a swap.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argues that a physiology-only prize is incomplete if drug development is considered essential, and that a one-part GLP-1 prize leaves CAR-T, with a similarly clear bench-to-bedside arc, unrewarded this year.
responses.response: Your two points pull in different directions and I treat them separately. On drug development, I have asked myself whether the achievement is the hormone or the medicine. The evidence of benefit on cardiovascular and renal outcomes belongs to the drug class, but the reason the class exists is the physiology. I therefore keep the citation on that discovery and let the clinical arc stand as its consequence. On CAR-T, I agree that it is the strongest second achievement. Pairing it would still require dropping a B046 name, and the CAR-T credit has the same kind of unresolved gap, since Eshhar is outside the credited set. An unresolved credit in each part is a poor reason to give up a settled one.

responses.point: Linnarsson names CAR-T as the next most robust candidate if priority in B046 cannot be settled, and argues that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer work covers one arc of the field.
responses.response: Your fallback is reasonable, and I would rank CAR-T ahead of B007 if the committee wanted a second part. I have moved slightly on Rosenberg since round 1. His adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is foundational for the field of cell therapy, but it is not the engineered receptor, so a CAR-T citation naming him would have to be worded around cell therapy more broadly. Under the three-person cap, June and Sadelain is the cleaner pair for a CAR-specific citation. My answer to the chair's question is that I would not put CAR-T in the prize this year in place of any of Drucker, Holst or Mojsov.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks cGAS-STING second and says that the Mojsov question must be resolved on the documentary record, not by leaving her off, and also that the citation need not mention any product.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and your argument on the documentary record is the one I rely on. On cGAS-STING my view is unchanged. The mechanism is clean, but no approved therapy exists, and priority is spread over Chen, Barber, Ishikawa and others, so I would not rank it above an achievement with demonstrated clinical outcomes. I do not consider that a permanent judgement. Ask me again when STING-directed drugs have produced trial results. For this year, the maturity gap is the reason I keep it below CAR-T and B007.

responses.point: El Manira notes that long-term safety of obesity indications is still accumulating and that B007 is narrower, with a smaller patient population and more weight on oligonucleotide chemistry.
responses.response: I accept your point on B007, and it is why I keep it as an alternative and not as a part. On long-term safety, I do not think accumulating data on obesity indications affects the discovery being cited. Randomised outcome trials already show benefit, and the citation concerns physiology and the active peptide, so wording that avoids any claim about the safety of particular drugs resolves the concern. I would read the committee's question on this as a drafting matter and not a reason to delay.

uncertainties: Whether the supplied record allows the committee to decide between Mojsov and Habener on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, which I cannot decide.
Whether the committee prefers to honour the physiology or the drug development in B046, and whether a majority would then replace Mojsov with Knudsen.
Whether a CAR-T pairing could be built from two or three names without Eshhar, and whether the committee would accept a pairing that removes a B046 name.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. I have no documented co-authorship, institutional tie or collaboration with Drucker, Holst, Knudsen or Mojsov, and none with the credited names on any other shortlisted ballot. My documented co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisen concerns other work, and none of it involves a shortlisted candidate.
